items.title: Cognitive Process Intelligence: Integrating Generative AI and Automated Workflow Discovery
items.abstract: Enterprises increasingly rely on complex, cross-functional business processes spanning ERP, CRM, ticketing, and legacy systems, generating massive event logs that conventional process mining and robotic process automation (RPA) tools struggle to interpret holistically. Rule based process discovery algorithms such as Heuristic Miner and Inductive Miner produce structurally valid models but cannot explain deviations in natural language, generalize across process variants, or adapt to evolving organizational vocabularies [1], [2]. This paper proposes Cognitive Process Intelligence (CPI), a framework integrating Generative AI with automated workflow discovery to bridge this gap. We introduce ProcessGPT, a 220M-parameter domain adapted transformer continually pre-trained on enterprise event logs, BPMN repositories, and standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, and augmented with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) over an indexed corpus of 1.8 million process artifacts. The system performs four cognitive tasks: event-log-driven process discovery, deviation and anomaly detection, natural-language-to-workflow translation, and automated process documentation generation. Evaluated on the BPI Challenge 2017/2019 logs and a proprietary 42,000-case enterprise dataset, the proposed CPI framework achieves a 0.95 average F1-score in process model discovery, reduces hallucinated process steps from 9.1% to 1.4% through RAG grounding, and operates at 96 ms average latency, substantially outperforming classical miners, sequence-to-sequence deep learning baselines, and general-purpose LLMs. Expert evaluation confirms near-human interpretability of generated workflow narratives, positioning CPI as a practical cognitive layer for enterprise automation.Originally published in Journal of Computational Analysis and Applications, Volume 33, Issue 8 (2024), pages 9173–9185. items.title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections
items.abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. Methods We systematically compared six deep learning models, including the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) series and the Detection Transformer (DETR). Three evaluation datasets were constructed. Datasets 1 and 2 (derived from 4000 hyphae and 4500 spore images) were used to assess image-level detection using sensitivity, precision and F1 score. Dataset 1 was manually annotated for the YOLO series and DETR; Dataset 2 (unannotated) served as the CNN series’ benchmark. Dataset 3 (1, 870 specimens from 1, 730 patients) was used to evaluate sample-level performance via confusion matrix analysis for the YOLO series and DETR models, employing medical records as the reference standard. The best-performing model was optimized and deployed into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform for real-time clinical decision support. Results YOLOv11 outperformed all other evaluated architectures. Detection was generally better at 400× than at 200× magnification. Notably, the F1 score for hyphae detection by YOLOv11 increased from 90.42% (200×) to 92.06% (400×). All models achieved higher accuracy for spores than hyphae. Patient-level confusion-matrix analysis confirmed YOLOv11 superiority. After optimizing an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.25 and the maximum confidence (Cmax) strategy, 200× hyphae F1 rose to 97.84% and the positive predictive value (PPV) to 98.27%. Subgroup analysis showed robust performance across different diseases, with tinea capitis reaching the highest F1 score (98.53%). Conclusion The optimized YOLOv11 model demonstrates potential as a rapid and standardized supportive tool for the microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections. Integration into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform demonstrates the feasibility of real-time AI-assisted fungal detection, offering a standardized tool to support clinical decision-making. This work supports AI as a potential complement to clinical and laboratory expertise, pending further validation in prospective and multi-center settings, and highlights its potential to streamline fungal infection diagnostic workflows.

items.title: Concordance Between Large Language Models and Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Recommendations in Treatment Allocation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Treatment allocation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly complex task that requires multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) input; however, its accessibility and reliability can vary across the healthcare system. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential clinical decision-making tools to aid MDTs. Our aim was to compare different LLM-generated treatment recommendations for HCC cases with MDT decisions. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 100 HCC cases discussed during MDT meetings in a tertiary-care hospital in Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Identical prompts and structured clinical information were offered to four different LLMs (ChatGPT-5, a customized Tumor Board ChatGPT, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Pro), each of which was required to provide treatment recommendations. Concordance with the MDT decisions was assessed across the first, second, and third treatment options. Inter-model differences were evaluated using Cochran’s Q and Holm-adjusted exact McNemar tests. Chance-corrected agreement was assessed using Cohen’s kappa (κ), and generalized estimating equations evaluated associations between concordance and clinical complexity. Results: First-recommendation concordance was 81% (95% CI 72.2–87.5) for GPT-5, 80% (71.1–86.7) for Gemini 2.5 Pro, 78% (68.9–85.0) for TumorBoard ChatGPT, and 63% (53.2–71.8) for Gemini 2.5 Flash; cumulative top-3 concordance reached 95%, 92%, 95%, and 86%, respectively. GPT-5 (κ = 0.754) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (κ = 0.743) showed substantial chance-corrected agreement. Gemini 2.5 Flash showed significantly lower concordance, including after adjustment for BCLC stage, Child–Pugh class, tumor burden, and treatment category (p = 0.006), while these clinical complexity variables were not significantly associated with concordance. Conclusions: LLMs showed moderate-to-substantial agreement with MDT decisions, with meaningful inter-model differences, for a complex disease, such as HCC. Our study highlights that, while the need for human oversight is essential, LLMs could serve as supportive tools for expert guidance in some clinical settings and underscore AI’s potential in enhancing liver cancer care.

items.title: Constructing Selves in AI ‐Mediated Apprenticeship Learning: Students of Colour's Narratives of Agency, Recognition and Negotiation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming computer‐assisted learning, yet little is known about how students of colour engage with AI within authentic educational settings. Existing research has focused primarily on academic integrity, efficiency and technological adoption, with comparatively less attention to students' own experiences of AI‐mediated learning. Objectives This study examined how students of colour in online apprenticeship programs constructed narratives of agency, recognition and negotiation while engaging with generative AI and what these experiences reveal about AI‐mediated learning within apprenticeship education. Methods A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 9 months with five secondary school apprentices participating in online placements across healthcare, government, finance, technology and public service. Data comprised repeated narrative interviews, classroom observations, digital artifacts and field notes, which were analyzed using manual narrative coding. Results Three interconnected patterns emerged. First, students exercised agency by strategically using, refusing, verifying, revising and disclosing AI in ways that maintained authorship and credibility. Second, participants viewed AI as procedurally fair while also recognizing that generic responses often overlooked their cultural and linguistic identities. Third, students negotiated tensions between AI‐generated outputs and institutional expectations through continual verification and adaptation, while proposing design features that would better support transparency, learning and equitable participation. Conclusions The findings suggest that effective AI‐mediated learning extends beyond technical proficiency to include learners' capacity to exercise agency, establish legitimate authorship and experience meaningful recognition within educational contexts. The study introduces Institutional AI Literacy and Recognition Bandwidth as interpretive concepts for understanding how students of colour navigate AI within apprenticeship learning and highlights the importance of designing AI systems that support transparent, equitable and culturally responsive learning experiences.

items.title: Continuance intention toward AI-driven mHealth apps: an extended expectation confirmation model based on a cross-sectional study of young Chinese adults
items.abstract: Background Cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have accelerated the global development of AI-driven mHealth apps, offering diverse functionalities to support personal health management. While China’s AI health industry has expanded rapidly within a collectivist cultural context, limited empirical attention has been given to how specific AI features are associated with users’ continued use of these apps, particularly among young adults. Objective Guided by the Expectation Confirmation Model and extended AI-related features, this study examined the factors associated with continuance intention toward AI-driven mHealth apps among young Chinese adults aged 18–34. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted, collecting data from 319 valid respondents. Data were analyzed using SPSS 29.0 and Jamovi 2.6.24 to evaluate direct, mediation, and serial mediation associations among the constructs. Results The findings demonstrate that satisfaction statistically bridged the indirect associations between core ECM constructs (expectation confirmation and perceived performance) and continuance intention, as well as between AI quality and continuance intention. Furthermore, bootstrapping analysis supported a sequential mediation pathway, showing that expectation confirmation was indirectly associated with continuance intention through the proposed sequential pathway of perceived performance and satisfaction. Conclusion The findings suggest that developers should consider the technical reliability and performance of AI-driven health management and monitoring functions to better align with user needs. Moreover, collaboration between health experts and industry practitioners may support the development of content for AI-driven mHealth adoption.

Guided by the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this cross-sectional study examined AI interaction and hypomanic persistence tendency among young adults screening positive for hypomanic risk. Interaction intensity and nighttime involvement served as stimuli; emotional contagion, emotion regulation difficulties, and sleep rhythm disturbance as organism-level variables; and hypomanic persistence tendency as the response. Partial least squares structural equation modeling estimated direct and indirect associations, including sequential paths; necessary condition analysis assessed bottlenecks. Both AI-use variables showed positive associations with hypomanic persistence tendency, stronger for nighttime involvement. Significant indirect associations were observed through the three organism-level variables. Emotional contagion showed a moderate necessity effect, while emotion regulation difficulties and sleep rhythm disturbance showed stronger bottleneck characteristics; neither AI-use variable was necessary. These findings extend research to naturally occurring engagement and distinguish association-based importance from necessity.

items.title: Correcting Health Misinformation Using AI Chatbots: Effects of Human–AI Collaboration Mode, Transparency, and Uncertainty
items.abstract: This project examines how the presentation of human–AI collaboration, scientific uncertainty, and supporting explanations shapes public acceptance of AI chatbots for health misinformation correction. Guided by the Human–AI Interaction framework grounded in the Theory of Interactive Media Effects (HAII–TIME), the study investigates whether these features independently and jointly influence trust in a chatbot, attitudes toward using it to correct health misinformation, and intentions to use it for this purpose. The study employed a 3 × 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment with a final analytical sample of 424 participants in China. Participants were randomly assigned to one of 12 conditions and viewed a simulated chatbot conversation addressing the false claim that insulin injections are addictive. Human–AI collaboration was described as human-dominated, with experts leading the evaluation and AI assisting; AI-dominated, with AI leading and experts verifying; or AI-only, without human involvement. Correction uncertainty varied according to whether the accompanying notice described the scientific evidence as broadly consistent or unresolved. Correction transparency varied according to whether the chatbot disclosed supporting reasons and sources. Analyses examined the main and interaction effects of these features while accounting for demographic characteristics, AI literacy, eHealth literacy, and perceived risks of AI hallucinations.

items.title: CrashSenseAI: latency-aware edge AI system for real-time traffic accident detection and notification
items.abstract: Road accidents remain a critical public safety issue, where detection often depends on witnesses calling authorities, leading to delays of several minutes before police and ambulances are dispatched. This study presents CrashSenseAI (CSAI), an Edge artificial intelligence (Edge AI) accident detection and notification system built on You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) and YOLOv12 models. Using a labeled dataset of accident and non-accident images, we trained Nano, Small, and Medium variants with batch sizes of 16 and 32 to evaluate accuracy–latency trade-offs. Results show YOLOv12n achieved the lowest inference latency (3.6–3.7 ms) with high precision (0.89), while YOLOv8s provided the best balance of accuracy and efficiency (Recall 0.85, Precision 0.90, mean average precision (mAP) at an Intersection over Union threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5 = 0.89) and mAP@0.5–0.95 = 0.70) at 4.8–5.0 ms. Larger variants improved mAP@0.5 scores (up to 0.90) but incurred higher latency (11–14 ms). CSAI captures timestamped frames with latitude and longitude, automatically notifying police, ambulances, and nearby hospitals to speed response and scene clearance, reduce traffic congestion, and improve victim survival during the golden hour. By combining real-time detection, geolocation, evidence generation, and automated alerting, CSAI demonstrates practical scalability for AI-driven intelligent transportation and road safety applications.

items.title: CRISPR dependency profiles distinguish pediatric from adult cancer cell lines via explainable machine learning: Identification of GPX4 and proliferative genes as therapeutic targets
items.abstract: Abstract Pediatric and adult cancers diverge profoundly in their molecular architecture, yet whether these differences extend to genome-scale genetic dependencies remains poorly characterized, with prior studies examining single subtypes or individual algorithms rather than a systematic, interpretable comparison. To address this gap, we tested whether Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 loss-of-function dependency profiles can discriminate pediatric from adult cancer cell lines, and applied explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to identify the genes driving this distinction. Chronos-normalized CRISPR GeneEffect scores for 18,531 genes across 1208 cell lines (242 pediatric, 966 adult) were analyzed; class imbalance was corrected with the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) within each training fold, differentially dependent genes were identified by Mann-Whitney U tests with Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction, and 200 features were retained by SelectKBest. Eleven classifiers were benchmarked under 5-fold cross-validation across 11 metrics, and predictions were interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) In this first (to our knowledge) genome-scale, multi-classifier comparison Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) achieved the best discrimination (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve [ROC-AUC] = 0.909, accuracy = 88.7%, Matthews Correlation Coefficient [MCC] = 0.632, Brier score = 0.089), with the leading ensemble and margin-based models reaching ROC-AUC values near 0.90. Among 3602 differentially dependent genes (FDR < 0.05), Integrin-Linked Kinase (ILK), Talin-1 (TLN1), and Aurora Kinase A (AURKA) showed greater dependency in pediatric lines, whereas Glutathione Peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and Insulin-like Growth Factor 2 messenger RNA-Binding Protein 1 (IGF2BP1) were comparatively more essential in adult lines. SHAP highlighted CHMP4B, IGF2BP1, GPX4, and LDB1, and the representative true-positive LIME case emphasized IGF2BP1, PAQR6, and CDS2. By exposing dependencies that adult-centric precision-oncology programs overlook, this work provides a framework for age-specific target discovery and prioritizes the pediatric-enriched ILK–TLN1 mechanotransduction axis for experimental validation.

items.title: Critical gaps in health technology assessment guidance for generative AI across six health systems
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare poses significant challenges for evaluation due to algorithmic complexity and evolving performance. Existing evidence generation guidelines, primarily designed for static medical technologies, may inadequately address the unique characteristics of generative AI. Here, we conducted a comparative analysis of evidence generation guidelines from six countries, examining recommendations for efficacy and effectiveness evaluations, health economic evaluations, social and equity evaluations, and uncertainty management for AI technologies. Across 56 documents, we found a consistent preference for randomised controlled trials and cost-effectiveness analyses, alongside emerging acceptance of alternative study designs and real-world evidence to accommodate the evolving nature of AI technologies. However, current frameworks lack specific guidance for the stochastic, non-deterministic, and adaptive learning properties of generative AI technologies. Moving forward, evidence generation guidelines require methodological and conceptual adaptations in order to improve the value assessment for generative AI technologies.

items.title: Cross-Scale Discovery of Surface Ligand-Modified Nanoparticles via Combined Transfer-Cascade Machine Learning
items.abstract: Abstract Surface ligand-modified nanoparticles (SMNPs), which immobilize surface ligands on nanoscale scaffolds, represent important nanomaterials for diverse applications. While surface ligands critically dictate the functions of SMNPs, their systematic discovery remains elusive. The major challenge in using artificial intelligence to predict and screen effective surface ligands and SMNPs across extensive chemical space is the scarcity of high-quality, standardized data sets. This impedes SMNP nanotechnology and leaves an enormous functional landscape largely unmapped. For antibacterial gold nanoparticles, available surface-ligand data sets are extremely sparse (<102), whereas public small-molecule libraries exceed 1010 entries. Here, we introduce a cross-scale (from small molecules to nanoparticles) transfer-cascade learning framework, called TRADE, that transforms the structural–activity patterns of molecular antibiotics into predictive principles for the surface ligands of nanoparticle antibiotics. Within TRADE, we chemically deconstruct molecular antibiotics into conserved scaffolds and variable substituents for transfer learning and combine a multitier, coarse-to-fine cascade to narrow the search space. We identify a new class of 24 surface ligands with high predicted antibacterial efficacy for decorating gold nanoparticles across over 9 million molecules. The leading auricidin inhibits bacterial peptidoglycan biosynthesis and demonstrates potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, with minimum inhibitory concentrations as low as 0.5–1 μg/mL. Across multiple animal infection models, auricidin exhibits exceptional therapeutic efficacy and robustness, superior to vancomycin, minimal toxicity, and low susceptibility to resistance evolution. This work proposes an intelligent strategy for discovering new functional nanoscale entities by integrating cross-domain transfer and cascade learning.

items.title: Customer Satisfaction, Customer Engagement, and Customer Retention Intent among Customers of Local Non-Alcoholic Beverage Chains in Valenzuela City: Evidence for a Customer Engagement-Satisfaction-Retention Framework
items.abstract: Customer retention has become increasingly important for organizations operating in highly competitive service industries. In the local non-alcoholic beverage sector, businesses continuously seek strategies that can strengthen customer relationships and encourage long-term patronage. Despite the recognized importance of customer satisfaction and customer engagement, limited studies have examined how these variables collectively influence customer retention within local beverage enterprises. Guided by Expectancy Disconfirmation Theory, the Consumers' Online Brand-Related Activities Framework, and Service-Profit Chain Theory, this study examined customer satisfaction, customer engagement, and customer retention intent among customers of selected local non-alcoholic beverage chains in Valenzuela City. The study further investigated demographic differences, examined the relationships among the variables, evaluated the mediating role of customer engagement, and developed a Customer Engagement-Satisfaction-Retention Framework. Findings revealed that respondents generally demonstrated favorable levels of customer engagement, customer satisfaction, and customer retention intent. Product quality emerged as the most influential component of customer satisfaction, while cognitive engagement was the strongest dimension of customer engagement. The results further showed that customer satisfaction significantly influences customer engagement and customer retention intent. Customer engagement likewise significantly affects customer retention intent and serves as an important mechanism through which satisfaction translates into stronger retention-related behaviors. The proposed Customer Engagement-Satisfaction-Retention Framework highlights the importance of integrating service excellence, customer engagement initiatives, and customer satisfaction strategies to achieve sustainable customer loyalty and long-term business success. The findings contribute to customer relationship management literature and provide practical insights for local beverage enterprises seeking to improve competitiveness and customer retention.

items.title: Data and Materials for How Should AI Voice Guides Explain Paintings
items.abstract: This project contains the de-identified data and supporting documentation for the study “How Should AI Voice Guides Explain Paintings? An Experimental Study of Guidance Strategy and Voice Persona Using Chinese Landscape Paintings.” The study used a Unity-based virtual gallery featuring six Chinese landscape paintings. A 3 × 2 within-subjects experiment with 21 university students compared three guidance strategies—Minimal Prompt, Standard Introduction, and Active Inquiry—and two voice personas—Warm Young Female Guide and Calm Senior Male Guide. items.abstract: This chapter examines decentralized education ecosystems by integrating blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the metaverse for next-generation learning. items.title: Decoding Workplace Behavior
items.abstract: The modern workplace is an intricate emotional ecosystem where human behavior, psychological well-being, and professional performance are deeply intertwined. This chapter explores the transformative convergence of artificial intelligence and emotional intelligence as a comprehensive framework for understanding, predicting, and supporting human behavior across professional contexts. Artificial intelligence is examined as an external cognitive companion that augments human decision-making and extends the practical reach of emotional intelligence into environments where direct human intervention is limited. Through natural language processing and computer vision, AI systems decode the emotional signals embedded in language, facial expression, and behavioral patterns, enabling meaningful prediction of workforce dynamics. Emotional intelligence is explored across three applied pillars — emotional appraisal, self-regulation, and purposeful emotional utilization — each carrying direct implications for leadership, collaboration, and organizational health.

items.abstract: The current high rate of adoption of generative artificial intelligence in higher education has led to a sense of urgency in the need to come up with immediate faculty-level literacy development. The idea of prompt literacy described in this chapter is a conceptual extension of AI literacy, focusing on the skill of developing effective prompts to achieve meaningful results in teaching, learning and assessment. It explores the current gaps in faculty preparedness and points to the absence of systematic institutional strategies to promote this new competency. The chapter also suggests faculty developmental strategies that are based on experiential learning, ethical awareness and continuous skill improvement. It also gives a detailed institutional framework to inform the systematic incorporation of prompt literacy into the faculty development programs. The chapter, with its focus on pedagogical and organizational aspects, will also help create a sustainable, responsible and context-sensitive implementation of AI in higher education.

items.abstract: Healthcare monitoring is an important area where technology can significantly improve the quality, accessibility, and efficiency of medical services. Traditional healthcare systems mainly depend on periodic hospital visits and manual monitoring of patients, which may not provide continuous information about a patient's health condition. The combination of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) provides an effective solution for continuous and intelligent healthcare monitoring. In an AI-based smart healthcare monitoring system, IoT sensors are used to collect real-time physiological information such as heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and other health-related parameters. The collected data is transmitted through an IoT communication network to a cloud or processing platform. AI and machine learning techniques can then analyze the collected data, identify abnormal patterns, and support early detection of potential health problems. The proposed system provides continuous monitoring, automatic data analysis, alerts, and remote access to health information. This reduces the need for frequent manual observation and helps healthcare professionals make informed decisions based on real-time patient information. The system can be particularly useful for elderly people, patients requiring continuous observation, individuals with chronic health conditions, and remote healthcare environments. The integration of AI, IoT sensors, cloud computing, and mobile applications creates a smart healthcare environment that improves monitoring efficiency and supports timely medical intervention

items.title: Designing responsible AI feedback in higher education: faculty readiness, student judgement, and metacognitive calibration
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now part of everyday academic work in higher education, including feedback. However, AI feedback does not automatically lead to learning. It can help students rethink a concept, improve a draft, and notice gaps in their work, but it can also create a false sense of progress when students accept suggestions without understanding them. This Perspective article argues that responsible AI feedback depends on faculty readiness and students’ evaluative judgement. Readiness is not mainly technical. It involves pedagogical judgement: knowing how to design tasks in which students work with feedback, compare it with evidence, revise with purpose, explain their choices, and remain responsible for the final submission. The article focuses on generative AI feedback and uses metacognitive calibration as a central concept. Calibration refers to the relationship between students’ confidence or self-judgement and independently evaluated evidence of performance. Evaluative judgement concerns students’ capacity to judge the quality and relevance of feedback and work, whereas calibration concerns the accuracy of their judgements relative to independently evaluated performance evidence. The article shows how ideas from feedback literacy, evaluative judgement, and self-regulated learning need to be adapted when feedback comes from systems whose accuracy and educational value cannot be assumed. It proposes a conceptual responsible AI feedback design cycle linked to assessment integrity, university policy, and faculty development. Although the cycle requires empirical testing, it offers a practical way to support reflection, calibrated judgement, and accountability without replacing students’ thinking.

items.title: Digital Archives of Feelings: Rethinking cultural memory and humanistic spirit through visual design
items.abstract: This article argues that as digitalisation and artificial intelligence become increasingly embedded in design practice, the preservation of cultural memory is shifting from physical spaces to digital environments structured by data and algorithms. While these technological transformations open up new possibilities for design methods and the transmission of cultural memory, they also introduce challenges: algorithm-driven rationality risks reducing the depth of human emotions and homogenising diverse cultural memories. Drawing on the theory of Archives of Feelings and visual culture studies, and adopting the concept of historical empathy proposed as a framework, this study analyses three key dimensions of cultural memory as mediated through visual design: social collective memory, marginalised group memory and human–AI collaborative memory. It further explores how visual design can negotiate between technological rationality and humanistic care, ensuring that Digital Archives of Feelings sustain diverse cultural memories while preserving emotional depth.

items.title: Digital Device Use and Hand–Wrist Disorders: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: The widespread use of smartphones and electronic devices has raised concerns about their impact on hand and wrist health. This scoping review synthesised current evidence on musculoskeletal and soft-tissue disorders associated with device use. Thirty-two studies were included, examining smartphones, computers and other digital tools. Smartphones were primarily linked to De Quervain’s tenosynovitis and flexor pollicis longus tendinopathy, while computers and visual display units were associated with carpal tunnel syndrome and repetitive strain injuries. Key risk factors included repetitive thumb movements, prolonged static wrist postures and extended daily exposure. Biomechanical studies confirmed increased joint loading and muscle activity during intensive use. Preventive strategies – such as limiting usage time, improving ergonomics, alternating hands and incorporating regular breaks – showed potential benefits, particularly when combined with user education. Most included studies were cross-sectional, limiting causal inference and highlighting the need for longitudinal research.

items.title: Digital information manipulation, AI readiness, and security outcomes in Africa: evidence from Africa’s most populous countries
items.abstract: Introduction The advent of generative AI has reduced costs, scaled up operations, and made it more difficult to identify disinformation and manipulated content, leading to new governance and security challenges in Africa. This paper analyses the nexus among the manipulation of digital information, governments’ readiness to adopt AI, digital connectivity, and security outcomes in Africa’s five most populous countries, namely Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, for the period from 2023 to 2026. The research attempts to fill a gap in the existing literature by addressing the lack of empirical research on the relationship between digital information manipulation and government AI readiness, and on its consequences for security issues in Africa. Methods The paper draws on the theoretical frameworks of Social Learning Theory and Routine Activity Theory and uses seven credible datasets, including ACLED, UCDP/PRIO, V-Dem, GSMA, ITU, the Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index, and Afrobarometer, to construct a country-year panel. Correlation analyses were conducted to test three hypotheses regarding the relationship among digital manipulation, digital connectivity, institutional readiness for AI adoption, and conflict fatalities. It utilises a verified multisource panel dataset spanning five countries and operationalises AI readiness as an institutional capability distinct from digital exposure. Results Digital manipulation was found to have a weak positive correlation with fatalities ( r = 0.23), a moderate negative correlation with digital connectivity ( r = −0.56), and a weak negative correlation with institutional readiness to adopt AI ( r = −0.42). These findings show that correlations between digital exposure and security consequences may be distorted by underlying conflict contexts. Discussion It can therefore be deduced that although digital manipulation is becoming an emerging security challenge, conflict and other structures are more significant predictors of security outcomes. This study offers an initial cross-national empirical assessment of AI-related security vulnerabilities in Africa and calls for stronger AI governance and longitudinal, event-level research.

items.title: DIGITAL LEADERSHIP OF OUTSOURCING IT COMPANIES AMID THE TRANSFORMATION OF THE GLOBAL MARKET OF TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
items.abstract: The article examines the essence of digital leadership in outsourcing IT companies amid the structural transformation of the global technology services market. It is substantiated that the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, cloud technologies, digital platforms, and agentic systems is reshaping the traditional determinants of IT companies' competitiveness, shifting the emphasis from the cost of human resources towards management's capacity to integrate digital technologies into business processes and to ensure their economic effectiveness. Contemporary scholarly approaches to interpreting digital leadership are analyzed, the findings of Ukrainian and foreign researchers are synthesized, and the place of digital leadership within the system of enterprise digital transformation is defined. The article explores the development trends of the global IT services market. It analyses the practices of leading international outsourcing companies regarding the adoption of artificial intelligence, the development of proprietary digital platforms, the enhancement of employees' digital competencies, and the use of AI agents in corporate governance. It is established that digital leadership is acquiring the features of a measurable economic category, since its effectiveness is assessed through the volume of orders and revenues generated by digital solutions, the productivity of managerial processes, the reduction of operating costs, and the speed of managerial decision-making. Particular attention is devoted to the current state of digital leadership among Ukrainian outsourcing IT companies. It is revealed that despite renewed positive dynamics in computer services exports and the active use of artificial intelligence tools by IT professionals, a substantial gap persists between the individual application of digital technologies and their systemic integration into corporate governance. It is argued that bridging this gap requires cultivating digital leadership as a comprehensive managerial competence to redesign business processes, deploy agentic technologies, develop employees' digital competencies, and safeguard human control over critical managerial decisions. It is concluded that digital leadership is one of the key factors ensuring the long-term competitiveness of outsourcing IT companies amid the transformation of the global technology services market.

items.title: Digital Marketing in the Age of AI-Driven Personalization and Privacy-First Regulation: A Conceptual Review and Framework
items.abstract: Digital marketing has evolved from a supplementary channel of promotion into the dominant mode through which brands identify, reach, and build relationships with consumers. Since early reviews of the field characterized digital marketing primarily as the use of electronic channels – search, email, and display advertising – to connect with customers, the discipline has been reshaped by two largely unanticipated forces: the mainstreaming of artificial intelligence in campaign personalization and targeting, and a parallel, intensifying shift toward privacy-first data practices driven by regulation, platform policy, and consumer expectation. This paper synthesizes the conceptual foundations of digital marketing with current evidence on these two forces to develop an integrated conceptual framework linking digital marketing channels, AI-enabled personalization, consumer engagement and trust, and business outcomes, with privacy regulation and consumer data trust positioned as a critical moderating condition rather than a peripheral compliance concern. Drawing on recent industry and academic evidence, the paper finds that while AI-driven personalization now touches nearly every stage of the marketing funnel and delivers measurable performance gains, its effectiveness is increasingly conditional on brand’s ability to earn and retain consumer trust in an environment of tightening data-privacy constraints. The paper discusses illustrative applications of the framework, outlines managerial implications for structuring digital marketing strategy in this environment, and identifies directions for future empirical research.

items.title: Digital Media Literacy in the Age of AI: Exploring the Comfort–Competence Gap Among University Students in the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates how citizens access information, making digital media literacy a condition for informed participation. This exploratory study conceptualizes a comfort–competence gap, whereby students report confidence and ease in using AI tools but a weaker capacity to evaluate what those tools produce, and examines it among 300 university students in the United Arab Emirates. The gap is advanced provisionally, and all measures are self-reported perceptions rather than demonstrated performance. Cross-sectional questionnaire data (twelve four-point ordinal items) were analyzed with ordinal-appropriate methods. Students generally reported greater confidence and comfort in using AI than capacity to evaluate it critically. Every operational item mean (2.51–2.55) exceeded every critical item mean (2.39–2.44), and the within-person contrast between the composite indices was small but statistically significant (difference = 0.12, p = 0.027, dz = 0.13), a pattern shown by 44.7% of individuals. No item-level contrast reached significance and 36.0% showed the reverse pattern, so the difference is read as an exploratory tendency rather than evidence of a general gap. The contrast is also sensitive to the composition of the operational index: with comfort removed, it retains its direction, but not conventional significance (p = 0.056). Digital confidence was the only correlate of comfort in AI-mediated communication (ρ = 0.131; OR = 1.29), a weak association in a model with minimal explanatory power (McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.012); communication competence and demographic characteristics showed no detectable associations, and parallel analysis retained no factors. Interpreted cautiously, the pattern bears on responsible AI use, since comfort unmatched by evaluative capacity is a weak basis for human oversight. The study’s clearest contribution is methodological: single-item self-report batteries can profile levels and detect aggregate differences, but they cannot show whether AI literacy is one capacity or several, cannot separate real capability from what respondents are willing to claim, and cannot support strong conclusions from null results. It therefore specifies the multi-item and performance-based measurement agenda a confirmatory test would require.

items.title: DIGITAL-GENERATION EDUCATION: INNOVATIVE DRIVERS OF TRANSFORMING THE MODERN EDUCATION SYSTEM
items.abstract: This article examines the distinctive characteristics of the digital generation, its level of proficiency in using information and communication technologies (ICT), and the challenges of adapting the modern education system to the needs of a new generation and the demands of the digital age. Digitalization processes are significantly transforming educational content, teaching methods, and instructional tools, necessitating the adoption of innovative pedagogical approaches. The article also explores the development of digital competencies, the effective use of distance and blended learning opportunities, and the role of artificial intelligence and emerging educational technologies in the teaching and learning process. Furthermore, it highlights the significance of digital transformation in improving the quality of education and preparing highly qualified, competitive professionals equipped to meet the demands of an increasingly digital and knowledge-driven society.

items.title: Digitalization of public authority within the paradigm of modern constitutionalism: transformation of public administration, popular sovereignty and the judiciary
items.abstract: The article examines digitalization as a factor transforming the exercise of public authority and defines its constitutional and legal significance for public administration, mechanisms of popular sovereignty, and the judiciary. It argues that the current stage of digital transformation goes beyond merely converting established procedures into electronic formats; digital systems are increasingly integrated into processes of information processing, the making of legally significant decisions, and the exercise of public authority. The article analyzes the legal framework for the provision of electronic public services and the operation of public electronic registers, electronic petitions, public consultations, and the Unified Judicial Information and Telecommunication System. Particular attention is paid to the permissible limits of algorithmic administrative discretion, digital inclusion, voter information autonomy, and the use of artificial intelligence systems in judicial proceedings. The author proposes viewing the digitalization of public authority through the interconnection of infrastructural, procedural, participatory, and guarantee-related dimensions. It is argued that the guarantee-related dimension is cross-cutting, encompassing requirements for legality, legal certainty, transparency, proportionality, equality, data protection, individual accountability, judicial oversight, and effective legal protection. The article formulates the principle of the non-loss of constitutional guarantees resulting from digital transformation, according to which a change in the technological form of exercising a governmental function cannot lead to a narrowing of the scope of an individual's legal protection. The methodological basis comprises systemic, formal-legal, structural-functional, comparative-legal, and axiological methods. It is concluded that digital constitutionalism should be viewed as an evolution of classical constitutionalism aimed at establishing legal limits on the use of technology within the sphere of public authority, ensuring meaningful human control, and preserving the human-centric nature of constitutional regulation.
